findings.title: a llama-swap release is trusted by its directory's name, never by the pinned digest it was checked against
findings.cause: install takes a release as verified when `<root>/v<N>/llama-swap` is a file (is_installed), and makes the pinned one current with no download and no hash; up (Inspector::target) runs whatever release `current` names from v267 on, pinned or not. Nothing records which digest a release directory was checked against, so a v270 or v271 that ai-ctl 0.2.0's `gateway install --version <N>` installed against the checksums file published on the same release page, which "detects a corrupt download, not a replaced one" (0.2.0's own DigestSource::Published), runs under 0.3.0 as if checked against the pin
findings.consequence: attacker: whoever can replace a llama-swap GitHub release's archive and its checksums file (§1, last row), before the user ran 0.2.0's `--version` on it; the control 0.3.0 states, the pinned SHA-256 as "the only source of trust" (docs/security.md:284, docs/commands.md:370), is never applied to that binary after the upgrade: `gateway install` reports it Reused or Unchanged, doctor says "v271, the release this ai-ctl pins", and `up` runs it as the gateway, which holds the key and every prompt. On this machine v270 and v271 were installed on 2026-11-07 21:00 and 2026-11-08 09:31, around the v270 and v271 pin commits (`feat(gateway): pin llama-swap v270` of 2026-11-07 at 21:01, `feat(gateway): pin llama-swap v271` of 2026-11-08 at 09:35), so no damage is shown: the control is weakened, not defeated
findings.fix: record at publish the digest the archive was checked against, in the release's directory (such as `v271/archive.sha256`), and have is_installed, set_current and up's target accept a release only when that record equals the digest ai-ctl pins for it; a release without the record is downloaded and checked again by `gateway install`, and up refuses it with `ai-ctl gateway install`
findings.test: install downloads and verifies again a pinned release whose directory holds the binary but no recorded digest (FakeGatewayStore with is_installed true and no record), where today it returns Outcome::Reused with no download
findings.evidence: read: src/application/gateway.rs:76-93, the `else if previous == Some(release) { Unchanged } else { Reused }` branches with no digest; src/application/lifecycle.rs:770-775, only `release >= OLDEST` checked; base src/application/gateway.rs at `chore(release): release 0.2.0` of 2026-11-06, expected_sha256 returning DigestSource::Published for any release but the pinned v263; `ls -la --time-style=full-iso ~/.local/share/ai-ctl/llama-swap/` shows v263, v270 and v271, the last two installed before their pin commits
findings.fingerprint: security | docs/commands.md + docs/security.md + src/application/gateway.rs + src/application/lifecycle.rs + src/infrastructure/gateway_store.rs | FsGatewayStore::is_installed + Inspector::target + Installer::install + top level
findings.note: the verifier's fix narrowed to the pinned release, the user's choice on 2026-11-12; sibling paths: doctor fails the pinned release without the record or with another digest, as up refuses it; the end-to-end test skips itself until gateway install records the digest; input class: no record, an empty or malformed record, another digest, a record that cannot be read; review-security's PROBE run at the user's word on 2026-11-12: the v271 archive's SHA-256 is the pin's and the installed binary is the archive's, so no damage on this machine; mutants M82 to M86 by hand

findings.title: an off-recipe build past the newest release can never be rebuilt, yet update and up's remedy both send the user to rebuild it
findings.cause: a build is past the newest release only when the remote no longer holds its tag, and the closing pass's --prune-tags makes the fetch that Builder::build runs before its checkout delete that tag from the clone. update_project still rebuilds such a build at its own tag, with force, and Configurator::runtime's refusal names `ai-ctl build <project> --ref <id> --force`. Both fail at resolve with "`<id>` is not a tag, a branch or a commit". The test that shows the rebuild succeeding relies on "the clone that made it keeps the tag", which the adapter no longer allows since the fetch prunes it
findings.consequence: the project withdraws the tag of the current build, say b12200, and the recipe has since gained a patch or a CMake option. `build outdated` says `off its recipe` and exits 4. `build update` fails with "`b12200` is not a tag, a branch or a commit of …" and exits 1, and so does every later run. `up` refuses the build and names `ai-ctl build llama.cpp --ref b12200 --force`, which fails the same way. No message names the command that works, `ai-ctl build llama.cpp` (the newest release, b12177)
findings.fix: in update_project, when the off-recipe build is past `found.newest`, fail without fetching. The message says the release was withdrawn and names `ai-ctl build <project>` for the newest release; or, if returning to an older release is now accepted here because `up` refuses the current build anyway, build the newest release. Make Configurator::runtime's remedy say the same when the build's release is not the newest. Change the test so its FakeSources checkout drops the withdrawn tag, as the pruning fetch does
findings.test: a_build_off_its_recipe_is_never_sent_back_to_an_older_release, with the failure asserted to name `ai-ctl build llama.cpp` instead of a missing tag; it fails today on the message
findings.evidence: reproduced: in a scratch repository, tags b1 and b2 in the upstream, a `clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout`, then `tag -d b2` in the upstream and `fetch --quiet --prune --prune-tags --tags --force origin` in the clone. `git tag --list` printed b1 alone, and `rev-parse --verify --quiet b2^{commit}` failed, which is the fall-through of GitSources::resolve (git.rs:99-114). Builder::build runs sources.fetch (build.rs:140) before sources.checkout (build.rs:145). git.rs:671-693 (a_tag_the_remote_withdrew_leaves_the_clone_at_the_next_fetch) asserts the same pruning
findings.fingerprint: bugs | docs/commands.md + src/application/build.rs + src/application/gateway_config.rs + src/infrastructure/git.rs | Builder::update_project + Configurator::runtime + GitSources::update + tests::a_build_off_its_recipe_is_built_again_at_its_own_release + top level
findings.note: the verifier's fix, the user's choice on 2026-11-12 to fail with a message rather than build the newest release; sibling paths: Configurator::runtime's refusal, doctor's off-recipe, smoke-test and unreadable-build remedies and Current::installed's error now name both commands through rebuild_remedy; mutants M79 to M81 by hand
findings.fixed_in: fix(build): tell how to go on when a build's release was withdrawn

findings.title: render_outdated and render_updated pad their columns by hand, a copy of the presentation's table
findings.cause: render_outdated builds rows of cells, measures each column's widest cell in chars and writes them two spaces apart, the last unpadded; render_updated does the same for two columns. presentation/bench.rs's `table`, shared already by bench.rs (6 calls) and compare.rs (5 calls), does exactly this, with a two-space indent and the line's end trimmed, which equals an unpadded last column
findings.consequence: three column writers to keep alike; a change to how ai-ctl aligns its tables (a wide character, a separator) reaches bench and compare but not `build outdated` and `build update`, whose output docs/commands.md shows
findings.fix: move `table` from presentation/bench.rs to presentation/mod.rs with the indent as a parameter (bench and compare pass "  ", which they print today; build passes ""), and have render_outdated push its rows and llama-swap's into it, and render_updated its [project, what] rows; each keeps its own rows, verdicts and trailing lines
findings.test: none: a refactoring under the existing render_outdated and render_updated tests, which pin the output and must pass unchanged
findings.evidence: read: src/presentation/build.rs:226-237 (width closure over rows, `{name:<project$}  {build:<current$}  {release:<newest$}  {verdict}`) and :278-295; src/presentation/bench.rs:424-443 (`table`: widths by chars().count(), " {cell:<width$} " per cell, trim_end); grep "table(" in src/presentation: bench.rs and compare.rs only
findings.fingerprint: refactoring | src/presentation/bench.rs + src/presentation/build.rs | render_outdated + render_updated + table
findings.fixed_in: refactor(build): share the swap standing, built projects and table

findings.title: inventory_projects copies doctor's reading of the projects the inventory builds and of those with no recipe
findings.cause: both map backends through `match &backend.source { BackendSource::Build(project) => Some(project.as_str()), BackendSource::Image(_) => None }` into a BTreeSet, then split it into the RECIPES it holds and the projects `recipe(project).is_none()`. They differ only in which backends they start from: doctor the backends a model uses, as `up` resolves them; outdated every backend, as docs/commands.md's `build outdated` says
findings.consequence: two definitions of "the projects the inventory builds" to keep in step; the difference between them (a backend no model uses is updated by `build update`, hours of compile, but not required by doctor nor run by `up`) is visible only by comparing the two closures
findings.fix: one domain method, Inventory::built_projects(&self, backends: impl Iterator<Item = &Backend>) -> BTreeSet<&str>, holding the source match, called by doctor with the models' backends and by inventory_projects with inventory.backends(); each keeps its own handling of the projects with no recipe (a failed Check, an Err ProjectStanding). If the cost of the method outweighs the eight lines it saves, keeping both is an answer, with a comment in inventory_projects naming doctor's different set
findings.test: none: a refactoring under the existing tests outdated_covers_only_the_projects_the_inventory_builds and doctor's build checks, which must pass unchanged
findings.evidence: read: src/application/build.rs:804-820 and src/application/doctor.rs:347-372, the same filter_map and the same `recipe(project).is_none()` split; grep "BackendSource::Build(project) =>" over src/: these two sites, plus gateway_config.rs:118, bench.rs:348 and inventory.rs:570, which use the project to resolve or check a backend, not to list projects
findings.fixed_in: refactor(build): share the swap standing, built projects and table

findings.title: build outdated and build update read the four remotes one after the other
findings.cause: outdated maps project_standing over the recipes in turn, and each runs its own `git ls-remote` to GitHub and waits for it before the next starts, so the command's wait is the sum of the four round trips, not the longest one; build update reads all four the same way before it builds anything
findings.consequence: measured on this machine on 2026-11-12, `git -C / ls-remote --tags --refs -- <repository> <glob>` took 0.70 s for llama.cpp (7767 tags), 0.69 s for whisper.cpp, 0.49 s for stable-diffusion.cpp and 0.45 s for audio.cpp: 2.3 s in sequence against 0.7 s for the slowest alone, so about 1.6 s of waiting on every `build outdated` with the shipped inventory. The cost grows with each project a recipe adds. On build update it is lost in the compiles, so only build outdated, a read-only check, pays it
findings.fix: in outdated, run each recipe's `sources.remote_tags` on its own thread with std::thread::scope (Sources: Sync, which GitSources, a PathBuf, already is), and keep project_standing's store reads and the warn calls on the calling thread, joining in the recipes' order so the table and the warnings stay as they are; or `none:` if 1.6 s on a command run by hand is judged not worth a Sync bound on the port
findings.test: none: the gain is a matter of timing, which the project's tests may not depend on; the existing outdated tests (order, one read per project, a failing remote not hiding the others) keep the behavior fixed through the change
findings.evidence: reproduced: for each recipe's repository and glob, `git -C / ls-remote --tags --refs -- URL GLOB | wc -l` timed with date: llama.cpp 7767 refs 0.697 s, whisper.cpp 44 refs 0.686 s, stable-diffusion.cpp 748 refs 0.486 s, audio.cpp 18 refs 0.446 s; GIT_TRACE_PACKET shows only `ref-prefix refs/tags/` sent, so the glob filters on the client and the wait is per round trip, not per tag; read: src/application/build.rs:779-782 `recipes.into_iter().map(|recipe| project_standing(sources, store, recipe, warn)).collect()`
findings.fingerprint: performance | src/application/build.rs + src/infrastructure/git.rs + src/presentation/build.rs | GitSources::remote_tags + outdated + project_standing + run
findings.note: not a local fix: the remotes read on threads need a Sync bound on the Sources port, its fake's RefCells made Mutexes and its call-order assertions made order-free, for about 1.6 s on a command run by hand

findings.title: each preload of a llama-server model logs failed to preload model: status 404, the model loaded all the same
findings.cause: llama-swap v271's startPreload sends `GET /` to each model of hooks.on_startup.preload through its local proxy and counts a status of 400 or more as a failure; llama-server b12227 registers `/` only with its web UI, which the recipe leaves out (LLAMA_USE_PREBUILT_UI OFF, the user's decision of 2026-11-05), so it answers 404 once the model is loaded
findings.consequence: each `up` with a llama-server model marked preload writes `[ERROR] failed to preload model <id>: status 404` into the gateway's log and emits a failed preload event, where the model is loaded and answers; a user reading the log after a slow first request takes the preload for broken, and no document of ai-ctl says otherwise
findings.fix: docs/gpu/llama-swap.md and `up` in docs/commands.md say that the log's `failed to preload model <id>: status 404` is llama-server without its web UI answering the preload's `GET /`, the model loaded; the web UI stays out by the decision of docs/security.md §7. Asking llama-swap upstream to count any answer of a started upstream as loaded leaves the repository, the user's call
findings.test: none: a document; the gateway's log of 2026-11-09 is its proof
findings.evidence: read: llama-swap v271 internal/server/api.go:400-435 (startPreload: `http.MethodGet, "/"`, `success := dw.status < http.StatusBadRequest`); llama.cpp b12227 tools/server/server-http.cpp:372-448, `/` registered only under `params.ui` with LLAMA_UI_HAS_ASSETS; ~/.local/state/ai-ctl/logs/gateway.log, `[INFO] preloading model: qwen3.8-27b` then `[ERROR] failed to preload model qwen3.8-27b: status 404`; the release notes of v272 read by review-dependencies name no change to the preload
findings.fingerprint: bugs | docs/commands.md + src/domain/gateway_config.rs + src/domain/recipe.rs | GatewayConfig::to_yaml + LLAMA_CPP + top level
findings.fixed_in: docs: list the gateway's open redirects and explain the preload's 404

findings.title: test_guard.py's child() leaves its process's stdout open, a ResourceWarning in a green run
findings.cause: child() opens the listener with `stdout=subprocess.PIPE` and registers its kill and wait as cleanups, never the pipe's close, so unittest's cleanup prints `ResourceWarning: unclosed file <_io.TextIOWrapper name=3>`
findings.consequence: no effect on the guard; the check's output carries a warning every run, beside which a new one passes unread
findings.fix: `self.addCleanup(process.stdout.close)` after the kill and wait cleanups, as orphan() closes its shell's stdout
findings.test: none: the check's own output, the warning gone
findings.evidence: reproduced: `python3 .claude/skills/reviewing-delivered-code/evals/test_guard.py` at `fix(reviewing-as-an-agent): give the driven programs facts a source` of 2026-11-11, 37 tests OK with `ResourceWarning: unclosed file <_io.TextIOWrapper name=3 encoding='UTF-8'>` from unittest/case.py:704
findings.note: older code below the floor: the skill's own test, from `chore(release): release 0.2.0` of 2026-11-06, which this roadmap did not change
